items.q: What should you remember about **Child vs adult plasticity**?
items.a: **babies are crude wide** webs; adults need gated neurochemical state shifts, not passive exposure.

items.q: What should you remember about **Hardwired vs plastic circuits**?
items.a: **heartbeat, breathing, digestion resist** change; sensory maps stay customizable.

items.q: What should you remember about **Post-puberty neurogenesis is minimal**?
items.a: **change = strengthen/weaken connections,** not adding neurons at scale.

items.q: What should you remember about **Recognition is step one**?
items.a: **naming a behavior/emotion you want** to change (even telling someone your voice triggers them) begins plasticity.

items.q: What should you remember about **Attention is the gate**?
items.a: **Recanzone/Merzenich**: bump-distance task rewired finger maps only with touch-attention; auditory-attention rewired hearing, not touch.

items.q: What should you remember about **Three neurochemicals required**?
items.a: **epinephrine + brainstem acetylcholine (signal/noise)** + nucleus basalis acetylcholine → change is mandatory when all three present.

items.q: What should you remember about **Alertness toolkit**?
items.a: **sleep, caffeine, accountability (checks to** hated orgs, public posts, love/fear goals — brain doesn't distinguish motive).

items.q: What should you remember about **Mental focus follows visual focus**?
items.a: **vergence eye movement shrinks visual** window → releases norepinephrine/epinephrine/acetylcholine; practice at screen distance before reading.

items.q: What should you remember about **Don't demand eye contact while listening**?
items.a: **visual system hijacks auditory** attention; closing eyes creates auditory cone.

items.q: What should you remember about **90-min bouts, not all-day focus**?
items.a: **warm-up flicker OK; middle ~1** h deep; Wi-Fi off, phone in other room; re-grab attention with eyes.

items.q: What should you remember about **Plasticity happens in sleep**?
items.a: **acetylcholine marks synapses metabolically; poor** sleep night 1 OK if night 2 deep sleep lands.

items.q: What should you remember about **NSDR post-learning**?
items.a: **20-min protocol or ≤90-min nap** after session accelerates retention vs waiting for overnight sleep alone.
